title: Finite predictive quotient and bridge descent
setup: Let S and T be finite transition systems on distinct carrier tokens, Π a finite probe family with horizon H, ≡_S and ≡_T equality of all Π-traces, and R⊆X_S×X_T a typed bridge relation.
conjecture: The predictive quotients X_S/≡_S and X_T/≡_T are finite and decidable.  R descends to a well-defined quotient relation iff it is saturated under ≡_S and ≡_T; if R also matches all admitted steps and probes, the descended relation is a simulation, and a bisimulation when both directions hold.
proof_spine: Construct trace signatures; prove equivalence; define quotient blocks by canonical signatures; show saturation is exactly representative independence; lift the step clauses blockwise.
finite_cases: MF-01 supplies a positive saturated bridge and a public-only collapsing counterexample.  MF-05 supplies an independent package predicate not determined by the quotient.
interactions: Feeds TH-02, TH-09, and TH-12; is limited by TH-15 and never supplies a full package or lineage by itself.
objects: finite transition system;bounded trace signature;equivalence relation;saturated relation;quotient simulation
lean_core: Equivalence and decidability; representative-independent quotient relation; simulation descent.
python_role: Partition refinement and shortest distinguishing probes.
circularity_risk: low if Π is declared before evaluating the bridge
falsifier: A saturated step-compatible R whose quotient relation depends on representatives, or a finite counterexample to step descent.
nonclaim: No full C-package, target consciousness, source lineage, autonomy, or personal identity follows.

title: Composition of typed predictive bridges
setup: Let R_ST and R_TU be saturated finite bridge simulations with compatible input, probe, and clock maps, and let every retained route-memory coordinate be part of the transported object.
conjecture: Relational composition R_TU∘R_ST is a saturated simulation S→U.  If a declared direct bridge R_SU is extensionally equal to the composite on reachable quotient classes, direct and factored transports agree; without route-memory compatibility the equality can fail.
proof_spine: Compose matching-step witnesses; use saturation twice; prove input/clock map associativity; compare extensional relations on reachable blocks.
finite_cases: MF-01 gives exact composition through a relabeled intermediate.  MF-08 gives a route-memory counterexample when a retained coordinate is omitted.
interactions: Requires TH-01; path-independent strengthening may use TH-03; TH-23 records the failure mode.
objects: typed relation composition;interface map composition;reachable quotient class;extensional bridge equality
lean_core: Simulation composition and saturation closure; compatibility law.

title: Route independence from trivial cycle-basis holonomy
setup: Let G be a connected finite route graph and every oriented edge carry an invertible map on a finite retained object O, with reverse edges interpreted by inverses.
conjecture: Transport between any two vertices is path-independent iff the induced action of every fundamental cycle in one spanning-tree cycle basis is the identity on O.
proof_spine: Reduce any closed walk by tree cancellation to a product of fundamental cycles; prove cycle-basis identity implies all loops act trivially; obtain path equality by closing one path against the reverse of the other.  The converse is immediate.
finite_cases: MF-08 is the one-flip nonflat witness; its compensating-flip variant is the flat positive control.
interactions: Supplies a usable sufficient-and-necessary finite flatness criterion for TH-02 and route-independent variants of TH-05, TH-07, and TH-09.
objects: finite route graph;spanning tree;fundamental cycle;edge automorphism;path fold;holonomy action
lean_core: Walk decomposition and path-independence equivalence for finite graphs.
python_role: Cycle basis and shortest nontrivial loop search.
circularity_risk: low if route memory O is fixed before testing
falsifier: A finite graph with identity action on the declared cycle basis but unequal path transports under the stated invertibility assumptions.
nonclaim: Flatness of O does not show that O is the complete consciousness-relevant object.

title: Acyclic local-witness gluing for an integrated package
setup: Let clause scopes form a finite hypergraph with the running-intersection property.  Each scope has a nonempty finite local witness relation, and adjacent scopes agree under their shared restriction maps.
conjecture: There exists a global witness whose restriction lies in every local relation.  If the family of restrictions is jointly injective along a join tree, the global witness is unique.  Dropping running intersection permits compatible-looking local records with no global witness.
proof_spine: Choose a join tree; extend a root witness leaf by leaf using overlap agreement; use running intersection to preserve earlier assignments; prove uniqueness by induction under joint injectivity.
finite_cases: MF-07 uses an acyclic clause-dependency cover.  MF-06 and a three-scope parity cycle supply local/global obstruction controls.
interactions: Feeds TH-05; isolates the nontrivial local-to-global content from the mere conjunction of C-clauses.
objects: finite hypergraph;running-intersection join tree;local witness relation;restriction map;global section
lean_core: Join-tree induction and restriction compatibility.
python_role: Construct join trees, solve local witness joins, and emit minimal obstruction cycles.
circularity_risk: low if local scopes and restrictions are declared independently
falsifier: An acyclic compatible finite instance with no global witness, or uniqueness failure despite the stated joint-injectivity condition.
nonclaim: The global witness is a structural package object, not consciousness or certificate soundness.

title: Staged heterogeneous package preservation
setup: Let a finite staged bridge carry separately typed clause witnesses from a stipulated source package to target-local witnesses.  Every clause map preserves its declared law, overlap restrictions satisfy TH-04, hard gates pass, and every final witness is owned by the declared target boundary.
conjecture: The final target satisfies the finite integrated package predicate.  If one preservation, overlap, hard-gate, or target-ownership obligation is removed, a bounded counterfeit exists in the model suite.

interactions: Pairs with TH-06 for autonomy and with TH-07 or TH-09 only if a separate lineage claim is desired.
objects: typed clause witness;staged bridge;overlap compatibility;hard gate;ownership closure;integrated package record
lean_core: Record construction from independently proved fields plus gluing and ownership lemmas.

title: Post-withdrawal invariant autonomy
setup: Apply a declared withdrawal operation to a finite target/control system, leaving only target-owned resources and an allowed disturbance class D.  Let K be a finite package-valid set.
conjecture: If every state in K has a target-owned response keeping all D-successors in K, then K is post-withdrawal controlled invariant and the package persists for every finite horizon.  If a reachable post-withdrawal state has no such response, a finite failure trace refutes autonomy.
proof_spine: Greatest-fixed-point characterization of controlled invariance; induction on horizon; shortest-path witness for failure.
finite_cases: MF-07 autonomous versus shadow target and MF-10 repair boundary; MF-02 target-only cycle.
interactions: Completes the A lane for TH-05 and the conservative SF-02 family; independent of lineage.
objects: withdrawal transform;ownership-labeled transition;disturbance relation;controlled invariant set;failure trace
lean_core: Finite greatest fixed point and induction on allowed traces.
python_role: Compute K and shortest collapse traces.
circularity_risk: medium if target boundary/disturbance class is tuned after the result
falsifier: A target-owned response condition holds but an allowed finite trace leaves K, or the claimed K uses a removed resource.
nonclaim: Autonomy over the declared model does not imply indefinite physical persistence, lineage, or consciousness.

title: Composition of finite causal-overlap corridors
setup: An overlap corridor is a finite support sequence with no empty process state, at least one nonredundant mixed-support update, signature preservation, and a target takeover boundary.  Two corridors share an exactly matched intermediate process frontier with no temporal gap.
conjecture: Concatenation of the two corridors is an overlap corridor from the first source to the final target.  The induced lineage predicate is relation-valued and transitive on composable corridors; it rejects MF-03 because the mixed/no-gap antecedents fail.
proof_spine: Concatenate stage sequences; preserve no-gap and signature conditions; retain a mixed stage from each leg; discharge boundary ownership and clock compatibility.
finite_cases: MF-02 is positive.  MF-03 supplies endpoint equality and causal provenance without a live mixed corridor.
interactions: TH-08 gives branching; TH-06 supplies autonomy; TH-22 shows endpoint equality is insufficient.
objects: support sequence;process frontier;mixed nonredundant step;corridor concatenation;lineage relation
lean_core: Definitions and concatenation closure; transitivity on composable episodes.
python_role: Find corridor witnesses and first failed condition.
circularity_risk: high if process signature or mixedness mentions continuation
falsifier: Two valid composable corridors whose concatenation violates a stated corridor condition, or a detached copy that satisfies all declared conditions.
nonclaim: The corridor relation is not proved necessary for consciousness or sufficient for personal identity.

conjecture: The induced overlap-lineage relation contains both source-target pairs.  It is not a partial function at the fork; any unique-selector strengthening requires an additional asymmetry not supplied by the corridor definition.
proof_spine: Apply the corridor predicate to each branch; relation membership is branch-local; invoke target-swap symmetry for the no-unique corollary.
finite_cases: MF-04 supplies exact symmetric targets; MF-06 supplies branch/fusion bookkeeping.
interactions: Consistent with TH-14; distinguishes structural branching from a claim of numerical identity.
objects: branched corridor;common prefix;binary relation;target-swap automorphism

title: Least heterogeneous predictive-ancestry relation
setup: Let H be a finite operational history graph.  Let Seed be an operationally defined source-to-target provenance relation, and Γ a monotone closure operator adding transition-matched descendants and declared fission/fusion consequences without creating a target pair ex nihilo.

proof_spine: Use the finite lattice of binary relations; monotonicity gives an ascending chain; finiteness gives stabilization; prove leastness by induction and isomorphism invariance by commuting Γ with relabeling.
